record.paper_title: Introduction to the Yang-Baxter Equation with Open Problems
record.context_brief: Minimal dimension for infinitely many YB operators
record.original_question: Determine the smallest dimension of a finite-dimensional vector space over the algebraically closed characteristic-zero field k for which there exist infinitely many pairwise non-isomorphic Yang-Baxter operators. A Yang-Baxter operator is an invertible solution of the Yang-Baxter braid relation, and the motivating existence result asserts only that some finite-dimensional vector spaces have infinitely many non-isomorphic Yang-Baxter operators.

evidence.quote: Theorem 2. There exist finite dimensional vector spaces for which there are infinitely many non-isomorphic Yang-Baxter operators.
Some directions for future research are: Finding the smallest dimension of a vector space for which Theorem 2 holds

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. A Yang–Baxter operator on a finite-dimensional $k$-vector space $V$ is a $k$-linear automorphism $R\colon V\otimes V \to V\otimes V$ satisfying the braid relation
$$(R\otimes \mathrm{id}_V)(\mathrm{id}_V\otimes R)(R\otimes \mathrm{id}_V) \;=\; (\mathrm{id}_V\otimes R)(R\otimes \mathrm{id}_V)(\mathrm{id}_V\otimes R)$$
on $V\otimes V\otimes V$. Two Yang–Baxter operators $R$ on $V$ and $R'$ on $V'$ are called isomorphic if there exists a $k$-linear isomorphism $f\colon V\to V'$ such that $(f\otimes f)\circ R = R'\circ (f\otimes f)$.

It is known that there exist finite-dimensional $k$-vector spaces $V$ for which the set of isomorphism classes of Yang–Baxter operators on $V$ is infinite. Determine the smallest integer $n\geq 1$ such that there exists an $n$-dimensional $k$-vector space carrying infinitely many pairwise non-isomorphic Yang–Baxter operators.
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches did not reveal a definitive determination of the smallest dimension for which there exist infinitely many non-isomorphic Yang–Baxter operators. While Yang–Baxter operators have been classified in low dimensions (notably full classification in dimension 2 over $\mathbb{C}$, and partial results in dimension 3), no source explicitly settles the minimal dimension question posed here. The status appears unresolved in the available literature.

status_evidence.title: Yang-Baxter operators - Encyclopedia of Mathematics
status_evidence.snippet: Classification of R-matrices is known in low dimensions; the general task is daunting.
status_evidence.claim: Classifications exist only partially in low dimensions, no statement about minimal-dimension infinitely-many result.

status_evidence.title: Involutive Yang-Baxter Groups
status_evidence.snippet: Constructions of infinitely many groups of I-type yielding infinitely many involutive set-theoretic solutions.
status_evidence.claim: Related construction exists but does not pin down the minimal dimension of vector-space YB operators.
